purpose: personal account of Alexey's working definition and perspective on the AI Engineer role

required_facts.fact: Alexey's perspective is based on around 15 years in software engineering, 12 years building machine learning systems, teaching, and regular conversations with practitioners.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 41: experience and teaching context are stated.

required_facts.fact: He defines an AI Engineer as responsible for integrating AI into a product and operating systems that can be evaluated, maintained, and improved.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 45: working definition is explicit.

required_facts.fact: The role includes translating product requirements into scoped AI problems and selecting and integrating models and tools.
Prompt design and versioning, success metrics, test suites, deployment, monitoring, cost optimization, and security are part of the work.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 54-57: operational responsibilities are listed.

required_facts.fact: AI Engineering overlaps with data science and ML engineering but focuses on integration, prompt design, structured outputs, evaluation, and reliability when foundation models are accessed through APIs.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 61-65: relationship and distinction are explained.

required_facts.fact: In established ML organizations, AI work can be distributed among existing members or delegated to dedicated AI Engineers.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 70-75: organizational alternatives are described.

required_facts.fact: In startups, AI Engineers often act as product-focused generalists moving from experimentation to production hardening.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 77: startup role shape is stated.

required_facts.fact: Key skills include RAG pipelines, tool-using agents, structured evaluation, monitoring and observability, and end-to-end system design.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 85-113: five skill areas and their details are described.

required_facts.fact: RAG work includes ingesting, chunking, embedding, searching, and grounding responses in source content.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 85-89: RAG responsibilities are specified.

required_facts.fact: The companion example moves from a simple AI feature in an online classifieds site to RAG and agentic systems.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 117: example progression is stated.

author_attribution: Present the definition as Alexey's stated perspective, preserving that organizational context changes the role and that it is not a universal title definition.
